lines.rhythm: PR lengthens beat by beat until a P is not conducted: Mobitz I.
lines.hyperacute: Broad-based, symmetric T waves in V3, V4, large for the QRS in front of them, no ST elevation yet: hyperacute anterior ischemia (an occlusion until shown otherwise). Repeat the ECG.
lines.lafb: Axis beyond −45° with qR in aVL and rS in II, III, aVF: left anterior fascicular block.

lines.rhythm: No P waves (sinus arrest); regular wide QRS at 32/min (20–40): ventricular escape (idioventricular) rhythm. The QRS shape shows where it starts: here the left posterior fascicle, with a left, superior axis.

checks: couplet: 2 ectopic beats (2 wide, 2 premature)

lines.rhythm: Sawtooth flutter waves at about 300/min, every third one conducted: atrial flutter with 3:1 block.
lines.couplet: Two premature wide complexes in a row: a ventricular couplet (three or more would be non-sustained VT).

checks: pvc: 2 ectopic beats (2 wide, 2 premature)

lines.rhythm: Sawtooth flutter waves at about 300/min, every third one conducted: atrial flutter with 3:1 block.
lines.pvc: An early, wide, bizarre QRS with no P wave before it and a full compensatory pause: premature ventricular complexes.

lines.rhythm: Irregularly irregular, no P waves, ventricular rate over 100: atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response (AF with RVR).

lines.pvc: An early, wide, bizarre QRS with no P wave before it and a full compensatory pause: premature ventricular complexes.

lines.nsstt: ST depression under 1 mm (or flat T) in II, III, aVF: a non-specific ST-T abnormality. ST depression of 1 mm or more in two contiguous leads would be called ischemic; here it comes from a narrowed posterior descending artery.
lines.avb1: PR over 200 ms with every P conducted: first-degree AV block.
